title: Guided filing journey — ANDS Studio
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar branded "ANDS Studio" and the subtext "· guided ANDS filing", with chips for "Help", "My dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry", and "Correspondence". Before Step 1, a "Before you start · external prerequisites" card appears, headed "Two things Health Canada must issue you". It states nothing on the journey waits on these but both take real time, and lists two numbered items, each with a lead-time chip: the "5-digit Company ID" ("lead time ~2 weeks"), enrolled by emailing a completed Company Template to the Office of Submission and Intellectual Property (hc.osip-bpip.sc@canada.ca); and the "Permanent Dossier ID" ("issued on request via REP"), filed as a Dossier ID Request through the REP via your CESG account, at most 8 weeks before you file. It notes you can begin with a placeholder ID and set the real one later, that validation flags the placeholder as an open risk until you do, and "You can reopen this from Help at any time." Clicking "I understand — begin the journey →" persists the acknowledgement and shows the hero.

The hero headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." A paragraph states an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make, and that this walks you through it step by step. You click "Start my submission →" (it shows "Starting…"); below is "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →" and a footnote "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

The screen splits into three: a left rail "Your filing journey" listing 10 steps (checkmark/"Done", "You're here", or a padlock with a lock reason); a center step card showing e.g. "Step 1 of 10"; and a right panel with a submission tower plus a "Readiness" card ("● BLOCKED" / "● READY TO FILE"), a progress bar, and a resume button. The tower has a toggle between "3D view" (default) and "Checklist" — the latter a plain printable table mapping each module M1–M5 to the Health Canada requirement it satisfies, its status, and outstanding items (Module 4 shows "not required for a generic ANDS").

Step 1 is an orientation form (e.g. "Tell me about your drug") that establishes your pathway. The company step asks for "Your Health Canada Company ID" (placeholder "e.g. 12345"); "I've requested it — flag as an open risk & continue →" turns into a persistent warning banner ("⚠ Open risk tracked… still pending… this reminder stays until then"). The dossier step validates the ID format on blur ("✓ Valid Dossier ID format."). The content step links "Open the Module builder →"; Continue stays disabled until the gate clears. Later steps run validation, a fees checkbox, QA review, and e-signature. Transmission leads with "Common Electronic Submissions Gateway (CESG) — Health Canada's official channel", noting CESG runs on the shared US FDA-ESG infrastructure, which is why a Canadian ANDS legitimately gets FDA-side receipts first; three receipt tiles "FDA MDN", "FDA ACK", "HC ACK (Core ID)" each carry a hover tooltip explaining that receipt. A Lifecycle panel shows the submission type, service standard (review-target days, on-time %), phase/status, review-target due date, and deficiency-response windows (SDN 45-day; NOD 90-day, 45 for DIN; NON within the window); a Sequences panel labels each leaf's new/replace/append/delete operator. The final step explains Health Canada's review timelines.
